A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StarGen work. All 13 pages of each are readable through extraction and rendered inspection. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains an appended reviewer-response page with experiments and clarifications.

before.justification: v1 reports original StarGen evaluations for sparse view interpolation, perpetual view generation, and layout-conditioned city generation, including quantitative comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds conditioning and backbone comparisons, higher-resolution examples, and 3D reconstruction consistency results on its appended response page.

M1.justification: The proposed spatial-temporal autoregression, reconstruction model, feature warping, causal compression, CogVideoX/ControlNet architecture, and three training losses remain unchanged. The appended experimental variants and selection clarifications do not revise the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: The datasets and three generation tasks remain unchanged. Longer ACID examples and higher-resolution runs extend existing evaluation settings; the added 3D-GS reconstruction serves as a consistency analysis of generated views.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are retained. The appended response adds a controlled comparison containing DUSt3R+ControlNet and DUSt3R+Concat with a CogVideo backbone, alongside StarGen and ViewCrafter with DynamiCrafter.

E3.justification: The main benchmark settings and training recipe remain unchanged. Added diagnostic experiments introduce 720×480 training, a one-spatial-image condition, controlled backbone/conditioning configurations, and reconstruction PSNR using vanilla 3D-GS.

E4.justification: The appended response substantially expands the diagnostic scope beyond the original component ablations. It tests stereo versus single-image conditioning, backbone and conditioning-mechanism effects, resolution-related artifacts, and whether generated views support consistent 3D reconstruction.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and the existing scalability curves retain their results. The appended response adds diagnostic scores, including RealEstate-10K FID 49.67 for one spatial conditioning image versus 41.72 for the retained two-image configuration, plus backbone comparisons, reconstruction PSNRs, and higher-resolution examples.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content, with notation adjustments. The appended explanation of depth-scale ambiguity adds interpretation of existing conditioning and losses, without a new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: spatial-temporal autoregression, three generation applications, and claims of superior scalability, fidelity, and pose accuracy. The added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of depth-scale alignment, artifacts attributed to low-resolution backbone behavior, and comparison fairness across video backbones. It also reports an unsuccessful DynamiCrafter adaptation attempt. The main conclusion's statement that 3D reconstruction has not been performed remains unreconciled with the appended reconstruction examples.

D1.justification: The response clarifies spatial-image selection by warping candidate depth maps into all frames of the current clip. It also discloses that existing ablation variants were trained without the removed conditions and provides lengths and overlap percentages for existing examples; these disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier experiments.

R1.justification: The same 81 cited works and main related-work discussion are retained. The response refines the technical positioning against ViewCrafter by distinguishing latent versus RGB conditioning, ControlNet versus concatenation, and the influence of different video backbones.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain intact. Changes include terminology and notation refinements, a funding acknowledgment, a backbone-fairness paragraph, bibliography formatting edits, and the appended point-by-point reviewer response.

P2.justification: The presentation is substantially reorganized: Tables 2–4 move beside Table 1 on page 5, Figure 4 changes position, and Figure 2 is redrawn with revised labels and visual grouping. The response adds compact comparison tables, reconstruction and resolution panels, and revised method diagrams.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional evidence about conditioning, backbone effects, and 3D consistency while clarifying implementation and resolution limitations. These strengthen support for the unchanged claims. The gain is limited by terse experimental documentation and incomplete integration, particularly the retained conclusion stating that 3D reconstruction has not yet been performed.
